title: A class that protects itself
description:
Write a class `Thermostat`. Its target temperature must always stay between 10 and 30 degrees, whatever the caller asks for.

- A new thermostat has a target of 20.
- `void setTarget(double degrees)` stores the value, forced into the range 10 to 30.
- `void nudge(double change)` adds `change` to the target, again keeping it in range.
- `double target() const` returns it.

A rule that must always hold ("the target is between 10 and 30") is called an **invariant**. Private data plus careful member functions is how a class guarantees one.
hints: Let `nudge` call `setTarget` rather than repeating the range check. One place that enforces the rule is easier to get right than two.
